questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a burning desire to come to Australia to experience the country, its culture, and the academic opportunities here, as I found the subjects offered here fascinating.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Absolutely the best decision I have made during my education. I have gotten everything out of it that I possibly could.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it has been fine getting in touch with the university. They have been good at providing information along the way, responding to emails, and offering online meetings where we could ask our questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mails, phone calls, online and offline meetings

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It has definitely been easier to get in touch with people once I arrived in Australia, as I lived on campus and the time zone difference was no longer an issue.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several different residential halls to apply for. Some more social than others (find them on Instagram when doing your research)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are no meal plans at Fenner, but there is a large kitchen where you can cook your meals and a smaller kitchen on each floor with basic kitchen appliances (toaster, microwave).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are several events and great opportunities to meet and talk with other international and local students. Additionally, campus life is probably the best part of Canberra, as the city itself isn't particularly exciting, but our social life across the residential halls was amazing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got into Fenner Hall, which is definitely one of the more popular ones. Fenner is located in the heart of campus—you can't get any closer. The place is very social; they have a café where you can volunteer for two hours a week, chat, meet new people, and buy cheap snacks. The hall has great facilities (a TV room, music room, and a lovely terrace with a view of Kambri, the heart of ANU). I can definitely recommend this hall. The room is small, though, and you share a bathroom with others. It's perhaps a bit old and expensive, but it's all part of the experience.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are quite a few introductory events that help you get familiar with everything. I found them very helpful, so I definitely recommend attending them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Honestly, I can't remember, which probably means it was pretty straightforward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mails, phone calls, meetings and that

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, they made quite a few changes to the courses I thought I was going to take, so I had to choose something else. However, I got into the courses I ended up selecting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stay updated on the courses through their website and keep an eye on any emails related to applying for courses and deadlines. The same course can be split into multiple sessions on different days/times, so you need to be quick to secure the session you prefer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked the subjects but not always their teaching methods

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is comparable to Denmark, but the teaching methods are different, which can make it more challenging in some ways. There are ongoing tests, debates, assignments, presentations, etc., that all count toward your final grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Honestly, I prefer the teaching methods in Denmark. A lot of the "teaching" consisted of pre-recorded videos from the lecturer, and then we attended tutorial sessions, which I felt didn't go deep enough into the material. Otherwise, it was fine. It really depends on your lecturer and tutor, and it varies from course to course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
THOUGHT LEADERSHIP IN ORGANISATIONS 

ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND INNOVATION

LEADING PEOPLE AND CHANGE

MARKETING MANAGEMENT

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you prefer. Sometimes, the quality of a course depends on the lecturer/tutor, and that's something you can't control. However, there is the option to switch courses if you don't like it.

questions.answer: The food is more expensive. I had to purchase extra time for my travel insurance, which was quite costly. There are also some fees associated with living in the residential hall, which added to the overall costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds. You can find it at their website

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are many social opportunities at the residential halls and as part of being a student at the university. Both creative and sports-related activities. There are large and small associations, so there's something for every taste.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve !! Black Mountain and the Botanical Gardens, which are right next to campus, the Parliament, Mount Ainslie, the museums, and Floriade.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
ChatGPT

They are very friendly and welcoming, but they tend to keep to themselves quite a bit. I think they're tired of making good friends who leave after just one semester, so it's all about charming your way into their circle anyway!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Learning to enjoy their version of a BBQ

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laid-back, chill attitude, friendliness, and approachability.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Enjoy every second of it and take some walks around campus and in the botanical gardens – bring a cup of coffee or whatever you prefer! 
2) Buy a disposable camera or something similar to capture some great moments. 3) There are many international students, just like you, who are excited about the upcoming semester, so everyone is very friendly and welcoming. Don't be afraid to approach new people and say hello!

and... 4) GO TRAVEL IN YOUR BREAK. Don't let money stop you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1) You won't see as many spiders and snakes as your friends will tease you about. That's only when you travel further north. That being said, they are in Canberra, but they tend to keep to themselves.

2) Be mindfull when packing. You don't need as much as you think. I arrived during winter and bought a cheap winter jacket from a thrift store, which I gave away. I also only brought 2 sweaters and pairs of pants, which I'm now lugging around here in the summer. There are also many thrift stations at the residential halls where you can find a free sweater or whatever you might need (including bedding and comforters), so take advantage of that and pack light.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made and the places I saw

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Personally, I haven't had any major challenges during my stay. One of the hardest things, I think, has been meeting so many kind people and experiencing amazing places, only to leave them behind. That's probably been the most challenging part, but it just means that the experience has been great!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Canberra's campus life is super charming. So if you come here, don't be upset about it. It may not be most people's top priority, but I'm so grateful I ended up in Canberra!

In addition, the application process might seem annoying now, but it's all worth it. Once you're there, everything goes smoothly, and I can highly recommend it based on my own experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
